Upscale Havens

Rommmates: Intentional homes for friendly roommates who like nice things

Given how awesome the right roomates are, and how hard the wrong match can be, it’s important to understand the systems that produce consistency and reliability. Multi-tenant and rooming house situations are complicated, and we have built systems to make our lives easier. You spend less time managing each other. Your landlord spends less time managing you, and we’re all a lot happier for it. Welcome to Upscale Havens!

Partners: A Values-Driven Approach to Living Well with Others

Upscale Havens helps small Canadian landlords maximize their return on investment from rental properties by specializing in rooming house automation. With rising mortgage and strata costs and a cooling rental market, it’s never been more important to find ways to save money. Better automation

Move-Ins

  • Ensure the assigned common areas and room are reasonably clean

Move-Outs

  • Check https://upscalehavens.ca/tmh/offboard to see the checklist they’ve already received
  • I will send you the Moving Checklist from Boldsign. It’s your responsibility to fill it out accurately and sign it with the Outgoing Roommate. You will get an email saying all parties have signed the form once they sign it too.

Maintenance Tasks

Electrical: Flipped Breakers

If a breaker get flipped, it’s up to you to restore power, figure out why it flipped, and send an email to the owner documenting the occurrence.

Loss of power can cause major inconvenience and in the summer or winter could make someone’s room uninhabitable, so it’ll need to be remedied quickly.

Caretaker Instructions

Showings

Start early: usually I start an hour and a half earlier. I use this time to go through the tour in my head and as I walk through the areas, I clean them and make sure they’re ready for the showing.

Start at the front door: Point out the shoe storage rack and how colors get used throughout the house to help us understand what we can use and how to keep it clean as our spaces are our responsibility. Head to the main floor.

 

Show the kitchen areas marked for each room including the fridge, freezer, and pantry.


Take them to the upstairs toilet: Mime and verbalize that when you come in you lock both doors and when you leave you unlock both doors. Mention the heated seat being great on cold winter’s days. 

(if you are showing Chrysocolla, show it now)


When showing any room: Point out the streaming services, the smart wall heater, the under bed storage, closet space. I will likely be getting an AC unit for it as well although the one currently in there is the current roommate’s.

Go to in-suite laundry: On the way, mention that there’s a lot of art on the walls because we care about the space and want to keep it nice. We’re looking for someone who also cares/wants to keep it clean and in good repair.

Show them the in suite laundry: Explain the magnet system.

(if you are showing Emerald, now is the time)

(if you are showing Diamond, now is the time)


Show the main bathroom: Mention the colour system on the medicine cabinet and towel rack. Mention the towels are for everyone but we expect folks to launder, fold, and return the towels to the common shelf.


Show the shower: Point out the over-head shower and the high pressure regular nozzle.  Mention the colour system on the in-shower bins. Mention the colour system on the towel racks.

Create A Roommate Door Code (Caretaker)

1. Shows battery life of lock

2. Instant lock control

3. Start here: Press "Passcodes"

4. Press "Generate Passcode" to create a new one

5. Specify a letter for the room a name (ex: D - James)

6. Press Complete

Change a New Door Code (Caretaker)

7. New codes must be used to unlock the door once before changing.

”8.

9. Make sure you're near the lock or it might fail.

”10.

11. Specify the new code and press OK.

12. You will see a confirmation it succeeded.

Delete Old Roommate Door Code (Caretaker)

1. Shows battery life of lock

2. Instant lock control

3. Start here: Press "Passcodes"

Skip steps 4 through 12 if you are just deleting an old code.

13. Press on the old code to access it.

14. Press Delete at the bottom

15. Press OK.

16. Make sure you are near the lock or it will fail.

17. You should see a success message.

Familiarize Yourself with Our Values

Accountability
“It’s okay that life happens. What matters is that you make it right as best as you can.”
  • Know where your guests are and if they aren’t back, go check on them
  • Any damages, inconveniences, or issues caused by yourself your guests, or your pets are your responsibility to resolve
  • Anyone at the property because of you is your guest
  • Consider how your behaviours are impacting other people
Communication
“People can’t fix what they don’t know they’re doing.”
    • When confronting a roommate, try to maintain a calm, kind, compassionate demeanor
    • Everyone makes mistakes but sometimes they’re unaware how it affects others
    • These rules also apply to your landlord, so don’t be afraid to let me know if I’m inconveniencing you or working loudly around quiet hours (I work late)

Respect
"Ask first!"
  • We foster an inclusive house culture that welcomes folks regardless of race, gender, sex, origin, religion, ability, or creed
  • Leave communal spaces better than you found them.
  • You may only enter another’s room, touch or eat their food, borrow anything of theirs, or give them a hug/touch them with their permission
  • Be aware of noise and observe quiet hours 11 PM to 7 AM
Kindness
“You can accomplish by kindness what you cannot by force.” – Publilius Syrus
  • We encourage direct, clear, kind conflict resolution
  • We support progressive improvements and work with each other
  • If they haven’t changed the behaviour, continue direct communication
  • Assume best intentions about other people. They probably are not trying to ruin your life by leaving dishes in the sink or making noise late at night; and they need to know it’s bothering you to change. Be polite and compassionate. If you don’t know how, ask chatgpt.com
  • We facilitate resolutions where necessary

Complete Before Move-In

On Arrival

1. If you need Wi-Fi, the info is on the side of the fridge.

3. Pickup your keys from your room.

4. Create and account and Sign into Signal. After you’ve put in your name and see your avatar, join our house chat. Say hi on the group chat. Join the Signal group chat. Next, create an account and sign into Signal. Finally, use this invite to join and say hi so we can welcome you!

If You Are Moving Out
Complete Before the Inspection
  • Bedside
    • Launder sheet set including pillow cases
    • Check mattress cover and/or mattress for staining
    • Make bed
    • Empty garbage
  • Vacuum/sweep
    • Floor
    • Window track
    • Corners of room
    • Any upper dusting surfaces, cobwebs
  • Cleaners
    • Dust or vacuum furniture (clean upper surfaces before lower)
    • Vacuum or sweep floors
    • Vacuum or sweep window slide trays
    • Mop floors
    • Wash windows and blinds or curtains
    • Spot clean walls with water
    • Deodorize room
    • Wipe baseboards
    • Clean window glass with cleaner

 

  • Common Areas
    • Remove all personal items
    • Clean assigned kitchen spaces (ex: fridge, freezer cabinet shelving, cabinet faces)
    • Clean assigned bathroom spaces (ex: item storage, shower storage)
    • Clean unassigned common areas: living room, bathroom tub and shower, kitchen floors
    • Clean door and wall messes
During The Inspection, You'll Sign This Inspection

A signable Moving Inspection will be sent to you by email

For Mid-Tenancy Inspections
Complete Before the Inspection
  • Tidy the room, closet, and under-bed area
  • Clear as much of the floor as reasonable so under-bed baseboard and floors can be inspected
  • Document all damage
  • Repair as much damage as you can
    • Fill any pins or holes in the walls
    • Sand the holes
    • Spot paint the holes in the walls
    • Spot paint any un-cleanable stains or damaged areas of the walls
  • Dust any upper surfaces including remove any cobwebs from ceiling
  • Clean any stains with water on:
    • doors
    • walls
    • window sills
    • desktop
  • Disinfect with cleaner:
    • Door knobs
    • Drawer pulls
    • Closet door pulls
  • Wipe with water
    • baseboards and door frames
    • tops of doors, frames

Privacy Policy

Who we are

Upscale Havens is a DBA for Intersite Consulting Inc. owned by Victor Salmon of Vernon, British Columbia. I was born and raised in BC, and seek to provide exceptional value housing for other folks who love BC as much as I do. My mission is to build a system for SRO (single room occupancy) rentals where everyone feels comfortable and safe, where the space is clean and resilient, and where the atmosphere is respectful and compassionate. I seek to eliminate the usual painpoints of roommates as much as possible.

Comments

When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select “Remember Me”, your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

If you have an account on this site, or have submitted data, forms, or comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service and some data may be temporarily held on or processed by our partner services like Interserver (our US-based hosting), Google, or Facebook.

This method avoids you giving more sensitive personal information out to each landlord and instead provides a landlord with your relevant credit history without info like your social insurance number.

This is the stage where I make a decision on whether or not we want you to be our new roommate.

The lease goes into effect once a deposit is received. This confirms your tenancy.

unsupported.detail: WordPress PHP never runs on static hosting. Any server-side behaviour (forms, AJAX, redirects issued by PHP) must be replaced by a static equivalent before cutover.

Divi inlines per-page critical CSS in <style> elements (19 of 19 pages). v1 styles[] requires an href and cannot express inline CSS, so DOM normalisation removes these blocks and their bytes are recorded by sha256 in capture/site-ir.capture-report.json. Until B1.3 materialises them as ordered stylesheet files (or the schema gains a v1.1 field), emitted pages will render without their critical CSS.
Fluent Forms markup is captured in the DOM skeleton, but submission is PHP. The form must be replaced by an island posting to a sink (B4.1) before those pages are functional.

Pages were served from LiteSpeed Cache (19 of 19). A client cannot force a cache bypass: `Cache-Control: no-cache` was observed to be ignored and still returned x-litespeed-cache: hit. Freshness is evidenced per page instead, by comparing LiteSpeed's embedded cache stamp with the REST `modified` timestamp.
Every <script> element is removed from the DOM skeleton, including Divi's menu/animation behaviour. Interactions that depended on them are absent until an island replaces them (P3).

capture.notes: styles[] and assets[] are empty by design in this pass: stylesheet and asset capture is B1.3, and a style entry requires the sha256 of shipped bytes. <link rel="stylesheet"> tags are preserved in every dom.html. Redirects (optional field) are owned by B1.6; the route manifest already records 11 proven 301s discovered during enumeration. site.locale is derived from the document lang attribute because /wp-json/ does not expose the WP locale.
